# A discount lands by three different rules, and each one posts a different
# pair of figures. GnuCash's invoice window offers all three in the Discount
# Type / Discount How columns, and a printed invoice has to state what the
# book posts rather than what quantity × price would be.
#
# Measured on GnuCash 5.10 for the lines below — 10 × 100.00 discounted 10
# per cent, taxed at 10 per cent:
#
#   pretax     900.00 + 90.00 tax    discount first, tax on what is left
#   sametime   900.00 + 100.00 tax   both figured on the full 1000.00
#   posttax    890.00 + 100.00 tax   tax first, discount on the sum of both
#
# INV-DISCOUNT-INCLUDED is the fourth rule that changes a figure: a price
# that already contains the tax, discounted by a value rather than a rate.
# INV-DISCOUNT-TWO-TAXES splits one discounted line's tax across two
# accounts, which is where a per-table-entry breakdown has to agree with the
# posting splits account by account.
#
# Every name and number here is invented.

2026-01-01 commodity CAD
	mnemonic: "CAD"
	fullname: "Canadian Dollar"
	namespace: "CURRENCY"
	fraction: 100

2026-01-01 open Assets
	type: Asset
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"
2026-01-01 open Assets:Accounts Receivable
	type: Accounts Receivable
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"
2026-01-01 open Assets:Bank
	type: Bank
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"
2026-01-01 open Income
	type: Income
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"
2026-01-01 open Income:Sales
	type: Income
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"
2026-01-01 open Liabilities
	type: Liability
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"
2026-01-01 open Liabilities:Sales Tax
	type: Liability
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"
2026-01-01 open Liabilities:Local Tax
	type: Liability
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"
2026-01-01 open Liabilities:Accounts Payable
	type: Accounts Payable
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"
2026-01-01 open Expenses
	type: Expense
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"
2026-01-01 open Expenses:Supplies
	type: Expense
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"

customer "C-DISCOUNT"
	name: "Discount Customer"
	currency: CAD

vendor "V-DISCOUNT"
	name: "Discount Vendor"
	currency: CAD

taxtable "ONE RATE"
	entry:
		account: "Liabilities:Sales Tax"
		rate: 10.0%
		type: PERCENT

taxtable "TWO RATES"
	entry:
		account: "Liabilities:Sales Tax"
		rate: 5.0%
		type: PERCENT
	entry:
		account: "Liabilities:Local Tax"
		rate: 8.0%
		type: PERCENT

# One account named twice in a table — a base rate and a surcharge booked to
# the same place, which GnuCash allows. It merges them when it computes what
# each account receives, so a page listing a row per table entry has to merge
# them too or both rows claim the whole 12.00.
taxtable "TWICE TO ONE ACCOUNT"
	entry:
		account: "Liabilities:Sales Tax"
		rate: 5.0%
		type: PERCENT
	entry:
		account: "Liabilities:Sales Tax"
		rate: 7.0%
		type: PERCENT

invoice "INV-ONE-ACCOUNT-TWICE"
	customer_id: "C-DISCOUNT"
	currency: CAD
	date_opened: 2026-02-01
	entry:
		date: 2026-02-01
		description: "Taxed twice into one account"
		account: "Income:Sales"
		quantity: 1
		price: 100
		taxable: true
		tax_included: false
		tax_table: "TWICE TO ONE ACCOUNT"
	posted:
		date: 2026-02-01
		due: 2026-03-03
		ar_account: "Assets:Accounts Receivable"
		memo: "INV-ONE-ACCOUNT-TWICE"
		accumulate: true

# Three lines taxed by three accounts, where GnuCash's own totalling and the
# lines' own roundings part company. Measured on 5.10: the lines hold
# 0.6294, 0.6000 and 0.1998 of tax, which round to 0.63 + 0.60 + 0.20 = 1.43,
# while the invoice's tax is also 1.43 — the sum of what each account
# receives, 0.24 + 0.48 + 0.71, each rounded once across all three lines, and
# those are the figures its posting splits carry.
2026-01-01 open Liabilities:Tax A
	type: Liability
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"
2026-01-01 open Liabilities:Tax B
	type: Liability
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"
2026-01-01 open Liabilities:Tax C
	type: Liability
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"

# Two lines whose tax splits evenly between two accounts and lands on a half
# cent each way. Per line, 1.10 at 5% + 5% is 0.055 to each account — so a
# page that rounds each line's own breakdown gives one account 0.06 and the
# other 0.05, twice over, and shows 0.12 against 0.10. The book rounds each
# account once across the invoice: 0.11 and 0.11, which is what its splits
# hold and what the page has to state.
taxtable "TWO EVEN RATES"
	entry:
		account: "Liabilities:Sales Tax"
		rate: 5.0%
		type: PERCENT
	entry:
		account: "Liabilities:Local Tax"
		rate: 5.0%
		type: PERCENT

# One line, two tax accounts, and a half-unit owed to each: the case that
# tells GnuCash's two possible roundings apart.
#
# 1.10 at 5% + 5% owes 0.055 to each account. Rounded per account, that is
# 0.06 + 0.06 = 0.12; rounded once over the invoice's whole tax, it is
# round(0.11) = 0.11. Measured on 5.10, `gncInvoiceGetTotalTax` answers 0.12
# and the posting splits carry 0.06 to each account — so an invoice's tax is
# the sum of its accounts', each rounded once, which is what
# `entries_fitted_to_the_invoice` computes. Every other invoice here reads
# the same either way, so without this one that model is assumed rather than
# pinned.
invoice "INV-ONE-LINE-TWO-HALVES"
	customer_id: "C-DISCOUNT"
	currency: CAD
	date_opened: 2026-02-01
	entry:
		date: 2026-02-01
		description: "A line owing half a cent to each of two accounts"
		account: "Income:Sales"
		quantity: 1
		price: 1.10
		taxable: true
		tax_included: false
		tax_table: "TWO EVEN RATES"
	posted:
		date: 2026-02-05
		due: 2026-03-07
		ar_account: "Assets:Accounts Receivable"
		memo: "INV-ONE-LINE-TWO-HALVES"
		accumulate: true

# Two lines alike in every field a comparison reads — same date, same
# description, same everything — so a block cannot be told from its twin by
# looking at it. The fit still parts them: each line owes 0.055 to each
# account, each account rounds to 0.11 across the two, and the odd unit goes
# to the first, so the page states 0.12 for one line and 0.10 for the other.
# That is what makes a block paired with the wrong twin visible.
invoice "INV-TWIN-LINES"
	customer_id: "C-DISCOUNT"
	currency: CAD
	date_opened: 2026-02-01
	entry:
		date: 2026-02-01
		description: "A line and its twin"
		account: "Income:Sales"
		quantity: 1
		price: 1.10
		taxable: true
		tax_included: false
		tax_table: "TWO EVEN RATES"
	entry:
		date: 2026-02-01
		description: "A line and its twin"
		account: "Income:Sales"
		quantity: 1
		price: 1.10
		taxable: true
		tax_included: false
		tax_table: "TWO EVEN RATES"
	posted:
		date: 2026-02-05
		due: 2026-03-07
		ar_account: "Assets:Accounts Receivable"
		memo: "INV-TWIN-LINES"
		accumulate: true

invoice "INV-EVEN-SPLIT"
	customer_id: "C-DISCOUNT"
	currency: CAD
	date_opened: 2026-02-01
	entry:
		date: 2026-02-01

		account: "Income:Sales"

		price: 1.10

taxtable "FIFTEEN"
	entry:
		account: "Liabilities:Sales Tax"
		rate: 15.0%
		type: PERCENT

# A bill has no discount column, so what it tests is the other half of the
# same rule: GnuCash rounds each line to the cent as it posts it, and a page
# that sums exact fractions and rounds the total once says something else.
# Three lines of 100.00 tax-included at 15 per cent post 86.96 of expense
# each — 260.88 — where 300.00 / 1.15 rounded once is 260.87.
bill "BILL-TAX-INCLUDED"
	vendor_id: "V-DISCOUNT"
	currency: CAD
	date_opened: 2026-02-01
	entry:
		date: 2026-02-01
		description: "First delivery"
		account: "Expenses:Supplies"
		quantity: 1
		price: 100
		taxable: true
		tax_included: true
		tax_table: "FIFTEEN"
	entry:
		date: 2026-02-01
		description: "Second delivery"
		account: "Expenses:Supplies"
		quantity: 1
		price: 100
		taxable: true
		tax_included: true
		tax_table: "FIFTEEN"
	entry:
		date: 2026-02-01
		description: "Third delivery"
		account: "Expenses:Supplies"
		quantity: 1
		price: 100
		taxable: true
		tax_included: true
		tax_table: "FIFTEEN"
	posted:
		date: 2026-02-01
		due: 2026-03-03
		ap_account: "Liabilities:Accounts Payable"
		memo: "BILL-TAX-INCLUDED"
		accumulate: true

# A second bill for the same vendor, so a selection can hold one credit note
# and something else — which is the shape the printers' filter exists for.
bill "BILL-PLAIN"
	vendor_id: "V-DISCOUNT"
	currency: CAD
	date_opened: 2026-02-01
	entry:
		date: 2026-02-01
		description: "An ordinary delivery"
		account: "Expenses:Supplies"
		quantity: 1
		price: 40
		taxable: false
		tax_included: false
	posted:
		date: 2026-02-01
		due: 2026-03-03
		ap_account: "Liabilities:Accounts Payable"
		memo: "BILL-PLAIN"
		accumulate: true
